premises.text: Consumer product companies lack targeting and waste half of marketing spend on the wrong customers
premises.evidence_span: they know 50% of that budget is misspent and wasted on the wrong customers. The trouble is, they don't know which 50%. And here's why. They have no targeting

premises.text: Smartphone barcode product check-ins with social sharing deliver friend opinions in-store at purchase time
premises.evidence_span: We want you to zap the barcode, check in, and then share it with your friends and followers on Facebook and Twitter

premises.text: Comic-book unlocks and sarcastic dragon quips hook users into product check-ins
premises.evidence_span: as you check into different combinations of products, you unlock these comic books

premises.text: Check-in behavior gives consumer product marketers the targeting tools they need
premises.evidence_span: By finally giving consumer product marketers the targeting tools that they need

value.text: Reinvent how consumer product companies market to customers with targeting wrapped in a fun game
value.evidence_span: we want to fundamentally reinvent how consumer product companies market to their customers

secondary_value.text: Consumers get hooked on a fun product check-in gaming experience
secondary_value.evidence_span: wrapping the whole thing in this fun gaming experience

causal_links.evidence_span: product check-ins that unlock a comic book adventure
giving consumer product marketers the targeting tools that they need

notes: Vision of disrupting the $2.2T market excluded per v1.3.2 §4.1(4). Fanship leaderboards and Quips folded into the comic/dragon twist premise per §4.1(5). Singleton D1/D3 retained: targeting problem vs tools vs consumer game are separately revisable. Coupon print volume treated as industry framing, not a premise.

meta.provenance_note: Codebook-only prompt v1.3.2; temperature not API-controlled in this harness.
